title: Verdant Healthcare POC — deployment mode decision criteria
summary: POC scoping focused on choosing between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Covered workload sizing, benchmark plan, success criteria (latency, cost, quality), compliance checks (SOC 2, KMS, SSO), timeline for a 6-week pilot and next actions to run benchmarks and share docs.
topics: deployment mode tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
workload sizing and expected TPS / tokens per second
benchmark plan and success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09 14:00 PT — Duration approx 64 mins
Attendees: Jesse Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SA); Dr. Aisha Rahman, Kyle Mercer, Renee Soto, Tom Basu (Verdant)

[00:00] Jesse: okay everyone thanks for making time, um, we wanted to run through the POC parameters for Verdant, get on the same page about whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense and nail the benchmarks and success criteria. rough agenda is workload sizing, security needs, perf targets, and timeline. sound good?

[00:22] Dr. Rahman: yeah thanks. high level — our use case is clinical note summarization and a triage chat assistant for nurses. mixture of short prompts and longer context windows — typically 1k to 6k tokens per request.

[00:38] Maya: ok that's useful, are the longer contexts full EHR extracts or summarized bundles? just want to map to sequence lengths.

[00:46] Dr. Rahman: usually a filtered bundle — maybe 4–5 documents concatenated so 3k-ish tokens on average, spikes up to 6k for complex cases.

[00:58] Kyle: on infra side we have Azure VNets and strict egress policies, we prefer VPC style private connectivity but open to hosted if data residency and encryption meets our rules.

[01:15] Renee: key compliance items — SOC 2 report, audit logs, customer-managed keys, SSO with SAML 2.0, RBAC and ability to limit who can call production models. Pseudonymization of PHI in logs preferred.

[01:34] Jesse: noted. Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II, we can provide the report; for keys we do both service-managed and KMS integrations in Dedicated/Private — hosted also supports envelope encryption with customer KMS in some regions. we'll attach the security package.

[01:50] Tom: from product side, success criteria for the POC are threefold: (1) latency p95 under 300ms for short prompts and under 800ms for average clinical requests, (2) throughput to handle steady-state 15 requests/sec with bursts to 80 rps, (3) acceptable cost — target is under $0.15 per 1k tokens at our expected mix. also quality checks vs our eval set.

[02:20] Maya: good to separate those. one nuance: for long context + generation the p95 numbers will move — we'll define two bands: summary (1–3k tokens) target p95 < 600ms; long-assist (3–6k tokens) p95 < 1200ms. is that reasonable?

[02:38] Dr. Rahman: yes, that split works. we also want determinism for regression testing — ability to lock model versions and config.

[02:50] Liam: that maps to rollout needs — Dedicated and Private allow model pinning and strict versioning controls. Hosted supports pinning to a specific model id for the duration of the pilot but there are capacity fallbacks we should call out — e.g., hosted will route to similar variants if capacity is constrained unless you opt into reserved capacity.

[03:10] Kyle: so can you clarify the exact differences operationally? we want a one-liner for each mode for our risk register.

[03:18] Jesse: sure — Hosted: fastest to stand up, lower upfront cost, multi-tenant, good autoscaling, ideal for early validation; Dedicated: reserved GPU pool for you only — predictable throughput and throughput SLOs, monthly commitment; Private: the customer-managed control plane (VPC/on-prem) with maximum data isolation, longer lead time and more ops work.

[03:42] Renee: how about audit logs and KMS in Hosted — you mentioned envelope encryption — does that satisfy our requirement to never persist PHI in Redwood-controlled logs?

[03:51] Maya: Hosted does redact or pseudo-mask PHI on request in logs if configured; however for full compliance Private or Dedicated with customer KMS is the strongest guarantee. we'll include the exact log retention and redaction options in the package.

[04:10] Tom: benchmarks — what does Redwood need from us to run a realistic pilot?

[04:16] Liam: two things: (1) a small representative prompt corpus (we'll take 200–500 samples across short and long bands), (2) traffic profile (rps over time, peak windows, batchability — whether grouping requests is acceptable). we also need a validation eval set to compare model outputs for quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or custom clinician rubric).

[04:36] Dr. Rahman: we can provide 300 anonymized samples and a clinician scoring rubric, that should be enough.

[04:44] Kyle: traffic profile — daily steady 15 rps, morning peaks to 60–80 rps for 10–20 minutes. some requests are latency-sensitive (triage chat) others can tolerate a bit more lag (batch summarization).

[04:59] Jesse: ok we'll plan benchmarking for steady 15 rps and peak bursts to 80 rps. for throughput we'll capture tokens/sec and request/sec, and latency p50/p95/p99. we'll also run the same test across three candidate modes: hosted baseline, dedicated with a medium reserved pool, and private in a simulated VPC (or using your staging VNet in Azure).

[05:20] Maya: note on batching — if your triage flow can accept 50–100ms extra latency we can batch to improve cost; but for the chat flows we won't batch. please mark requests as latency-sensitive vs batchable in the profile CSV.

[05:34] Renee: what's the timeline if we choose Dedicated vs Private? we have a three-month window to production ideally.

[05:41] Jesse: Dedicated: about 2–3 weeks to provision reserved capacity and run pilot tests; Private (VPC) is typically 6–8 weeks because of network setup, peering, and security review. Hosted is immediate — couple days for credentials and configs.

[05:57] Tom: that week delta is OK. we need clear gating criteria for moving from pilot to full rollout — apart from perf, compliance sign-offs required from security and legal.

[06:08] Liam: recommended gating checklist: meet perf targets on your eval set; success on quality regression tests (no >5% drop vs baseline metrics), cost modeling within target budget, SOC2/contract terms agreed, and ops runbook validated (autoscaling and fallback behaviours tested).

[06:28] Dr. Rahman: what about model updates — how do rollouts work? we want canary testing and quick rollback.

[06:35] Maya: we support A/B and canary rollouts across all modes. Dedicated and Private give you more granular control over the kernel versions and quantization profiles. Hosted will allow canaries but the degree of isolation depends on capacity; we'll show the rollout controls in the console demo.

[06:55] Kyle: cost question again — can you ballpark expected monthly infra cost for handling 15 steady rps with peaks? assume mix is 70% short prompts, 30% long.

[07:06] Jesse: rough order: Hosted: $X — we shouldn't put a number on a recording, but we'll follow up with a model-specific cost sheet. for planning though, expect Dedicated to have higher baseline but lower per-token marginal cost. We'll run benchmark and produce per-1k-token cost breakdown.

[07:24] Tom: understood. can you also measure cold start times and KV cache warmup effects? our workflow uses persistent sessions.

[07:31] Maya: yes we'll measure warm vs cold for KV cache hit rates and effective latency. we can instrument prefix caching and show how effective serving reduces per-token cost after warm up.

[07:44] Renee: security follow-ups — we need specifics on encryption at rest in each mode, whether logs contain prompt text, and SAML SSO integration details.

[07:52] Jesse: action: we'll attach a security one-pager with SOC2 attestations, KMS details, SAML config guide, and log retention options.

[08:02] Dr. Rahman: good. now what about the actual benchmark run plan and responsibilities?

[08:08] Liam: plan: week 0 (this week) — exchange prompt corpus, traffic profile, and eval rubric. Week 1–2 — Redwood runs hosted baseline and shares results. Week 3 — Redwood provisions Dedicated (medium pool) and runs the same tests. Week 4–5 — simulated Private or staging VNet run + security review. Week 6 — analyze results, sync and decision. if Dedicated looks good we can shorten to 4 weeks.

[08:36] Kyle: can Redwood run tests from our VNet for the Private sim? we prefer not to share real PHI during testing.

[08:42] Maya: yes we can run tests against a staging VNet and we can also run synthetic but realistic loads. recommend anonymized/hashed samples.

[08:52] Dr. Rahman: quality thresholds — on our rubric clinicians won't accept more than 10% hallucinations in summaries. how do you define hallucination in scoring?

[09:01] Jesse: let's define a binary clinical hallucination flag per example (0/1) plus severity (low/moderate/high). we'll produce aggregated rates. if >10% severe by your rubric that's fail.

[09:14] Tom: what telemetry will you provide during the pilot? we want per-request token counts, latency, model version, KV cache hit/miss, and cost estimate.

[09:25] Liam: the Console will provide token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and a CSV export with request-level rows. we'll enable tracing hooks for a subset of requests for deeper root cause.

[09:36] Renee: on legal — we need a standard DPA and data residency clause for the pilot; is that standard?

[09:42] Jesse: yes we can share a pilot DPA. for Dedicated/private we can include stronger residency and deletion clauses. we'll have legal loop in once you see the security package.

[09:52] Dr. Rahman: competitor note — we've looked at two other vendors (DocStream AI and CoreInference). we like Redwood's runtime optimizations but want to validate the claimed p95 numbers.

[10:05] Maya: understood, we'll run head-to-head benchmarks vs a configured open model on similar infra if you want; that usually gives a clear apples-to-apples.

[10:15] Jesse: ok to capture action items and next steps. any remaining questions?

[10:21] Tom: one last on burst handling — if we get 80 rps bursts, what's the fallback behavior? we don't want dropped requests.

[10:28] Liam: fallback policies: hosted can fall back to a smaller but compatible model variant or queue with graceful degradation. Dedicated can burst into shared capacity if you opt-in to burst credits, and Private we typically tune autoscaling and pre-warm pools. we'll surface the policy and test it during bench runs.

[10:45] Dr. Rahman: perfect. thanks everyone. Jesse, can you send the timeline and the checklist?

[10:51] Jesse: yes I'll send the security bundle and the scaffold for the benchmark. we'll schedule the technical deep dive to provision Dedicated if you decide to go that route.

[10:58] Renee: thanks, looking forward to docs.

[11:00] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — "VPC" was sometimes captured as "V-P-C P" in our raw capture. Speaker tags partially cleaned. Some acronyms may be mis-cased.
action_items: Redwood (Jesse/Maya): Send security one-pager, SOC2 report, SAML/KMS integration guide — due 2026-12-11
Verdant (Aisha/Kyle): Share anonymized prompt corpus (300 samples), traffic profile CSV, and clinician scoring rubric — due 2026-12-12
Redwood (Liam): Run hosted baseline benchmark using provided corpus and share results + per-1k-token cost breakdown — due 2026-12-16
Redwood: Provision Dedicated medium pool and run comparative benchmark (if approved) — target start 2026-12-20
All: Schedule technical deep dive for Dedicated provisioning and network peering — proposed 2026-12-18
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and pilot DPA
Verdant to provide corpus and traffic profile
Redwood to perform hosted baseline benchmarks and report results
Plan decision sync week of 2026-12-21 to review results and choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
